steps.intro: You asked for the specifics of what future chats ask you and what they decide alone.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Is this the right three-way split?
steps.today: Written rules tell chats how to build a deck. None says which decisions are yours. My earlier "nothing written down" was too loose: the how is written, the who is not.
steps.problem: Without it, one chat asks you about build details and the next silently changes how a screen behaves.
steps.proposal: ASKED, with options: anything a user sees or feels. Layout, on-screen words, what a control does, step order, noticeable defaults, what happens on failure, anything removed, anything costing money or privacy. LISTED as calls you can overrule: visible choices with one obvious answer from the design guide. NEVER SHOWN: build details no user can notice.

options.label: This three-way split
pros: Big decisions stay yours; small ones cannot surprise you.
Fewer questions per deck.
cons: A chat can misjudge "obvious" and list something you wanted to be asked.

options.label: Ask more: listed calls become questions
pros: Nothing visible stands without your direct answer.
cons: Longer decks; big decisions get buried again.

options.label: Ask less: only layout and behaviour are asked
pros: Shortest decks.
cons: Words, defaults and failure handling get decided for you.

steps.checked: Read all three rule files and the deck guide on 9 Nov. They cover kinds, fields and commands. None says who decides what.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: When a chat is unsure which group a decision belongs in, what should it do?
steps.problem: Guessing "small" hides a decision from you. Guessing "big" pads the deck.
steps.proposal: When unsure, ask it as a question.

options.label: Ask it as a question
pros: You never lose a decision to a wrong guess.
cons: Some decks carry a question you find trivial.

options.label: Put it in the calls list
pros: Shorter decks.
cons: You must read the list carefully every time.

steps.page: The walkthrough that replaces the contract
steps.intro: You picked "before and after building" and wanted to steer the design further.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Are these the right six parts, in this order?
steps.today: The drawing shows two of the parts. Nothing is built yet.
steps.problem: You said the contract did a poor job of showing what exists, how parts fit and how it is tested.
steps.proposal: 1 What this is for. 2 Every screen: its picture and the decision of yours behind it. 3 Behind the scenes, as numbered plain steps. 4 Calls I made. 5 Checks. 6 Left for you to verify yourself. Drag on the drawing to change any part of it.

options.label: These six, this order
pros: Reads start to finish like a tour of the feature.
cons: A big feature makes a long deck.

options.label: Screens first, purpose folded into the opening screen
pros: You see the thing sooner.
cons: No single place states what the feature is for.

steps.caption: A drawing of parts 2 and 3. Drag on it to comment on an area.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: How should you answer each item in a walkthrough?
steps.today: Today a screen gets Yes or No, and a contract row gets nothing of its own.
steps.problem: A walkthrough has dozens of items. Yes or No on each is slow, and one Yes for the whole deck is the rubber stamp you disliked.
steps.proposal: Every item works like the calls list on the previous page: it stands unless you press Change this, which opens its own box. Pictures also take dragged areas.

options.label: Stands unless you press Change this
pros: Fast when things are right; precise when they are not.
cons: An item you skimmed past counts as accepted.

options.label: A Yes or No on every item
pros: Nothing is accepted without a deliberate press.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Is this how the Checks part should work?
steps.today: An independent reviewer runs a fixed routine you did not choose, and you see a pass or fail table.
steps.problem: You want to direct the checks yourself, and see proof.
steps.proposal: Before building: I suggest a handful of checks with reasons; you tick the ones to run and say any of your own in words. After building: each check shows pass, fail or unclear with its picture or clip, then a short list of things only you can verify.

options.label: You choose the checks, I show proof
pros: You direct exactly what gets tested.
Proof is a picture or clip, not a word.
cons: More checks ticked means a slower, costlier build.

options.label: Same, but show proof only for failures
pros: Shorter results.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Is this the finish line?
steps.today: A feature is blocked from finishing until a contract is signed and graded.
steps.problem: You skip both, so the block guards steps you do not use.
steps.proposal: Finished means: every change you asked for is in the before-build walkthrough, and you submitted the after-build walkthrough with nothing marked Change. If you mark anything, I fix it and the same deck returns showing only what changed.

options.label: Yes, that is the finish line
pros: One clear rule you control.
cons: A small fix sends the deck back to you once more.

options.label: Same, but tiny fixes do not need a return trip
pros: Fewer round trips.
cons: You do not see the fix before it counts as finished.

steps.page: One deck that grows, instead of many

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: When I revise a deck after your answers, how should the same deck show it?
steps.today: Each round is a new deck with a new link. Earlier answers live in separate files.
steps.problem: One feature reached 108 decks. You lose track of what you already said.
steps.proposal: One link per topic. Reopened, it leads with what is new or changed, each marked New. Settled questions fold up below with your answer shown. Earlier wording and answers sit in a History view. Truly different topics still get their own deck.

options.label: New first, settled folded below, History view
pros: You only read what changed.
Your earlier answers are always in sight.

options.label: Everything stays in place, changed ones get a badge
pros: Nothing moves.
cons: You scroll past settled questions to find new ones.

steps.problem: You asked for a way to track decks that are related but separate.

options.label: Add the Related list
pros: You can hop between connected decks.
cons: One more thing in the header area.

options.label: Leave it
pros: Nothing added.
cons: You keep asking chat where the other deck is.
